title: Why Is This Moroccan Town Painted Blue?
hook: In Morocco's Rif Mountains, a whole town is painted blue, and nobody agrees why.
voiceoverScript: In Morocco's Rif Mountains, a whole town is painted blue, and nobody agrees why. Chefchaouen began in 1471 as a small fortress in northern Morocco. Its old medina still climbs the hillside in narrow lanes. The famous blue came much later. One popular story credits Jewish families who settled here in the 1930s, linking blue with the sky. Others say the colour keeps homes cool or keeps mosquitoes away. Some simply say it looks beautiful, and it certainly draws visitors. Residents still repaint their walls regularly, keeping every shade of blue fresh for the next generation. Follow Savannah Atlas for more places worth discovering.
